output.headline: Veritas Capital offers a technology-focused sponsor with a Health IT precedent and a 25.3% return at the asking price, though size is a stretch.
output.differentiator: Highest close rate among the financial sponsors on the priority list (15 of 16, 94%), and its returns analysis clears the 20% hurdle at the asking price, with room to pay up to $356M.
output.why_them: Technology mandate sponsor; closes deals; clears 20% IRR at ask

acquirer_overview.title: A technology-mandate sponsor that closes nearly everything it signs
points: Financial sponsor with 16 deals from 2015 to 2024; 15 closed (94%) and 14 were control deals rather than minority stakes. [T:record, K:closed_share, K:control_share]
Mandate: technology or technology-enabled solutions to government and commercial customers; $50B+ AUM across 3 strategies, including committed capital. [P:1, P:2]
Mostly outside Health IT: 15 of 16 deals, with 1 in the target's own sub-sector and none in adjacent Health IT sub-sectors. [T:record]

strategic_fit_thesis.title: A Health IT bolt-on precedent and a technology mandate, but a thin sector record
points: Platform Build in 8 of 16 deals, against 23% of all deals in the file, is its most distinctive motive. [M:platform_build]
Bought Great Health Informatics ($29M, 2020, bolt-on) in the target's own sub-sector; its mandate covers technology-enabled solutions. [D:MA-2020-0309, P:1]
Share of deals closed is a modest factor for; geography and deal size are slight factors for; margin fit is slightly against. [S:close_rate_s, S:geo_fit, S:not_smaller, S:margin_fit]

precedent_activity.title: One Health IT bolt-on, plus revenue cycle deals at up to 21.0x
points: Great Health Informatics: $29M bolt-on, 2020, 20.3x EBITDA, closed; same sub-sector as the target. [D:MA-2020-0309]
Revenue cycle: Great Reimbursement ($26M, 2022, 21.0x) and Granite RCM ($34M, 2019, 14.5x), both closed. [D:MA-2022-0294, D:MA-2019-0088]
Crown Mental Health: $453M recapitalization, 2024, 8.6x. Only 2 of 16 deals fall in the $150M-$600M size band. [D:MA-2024-0079, K:size_band]

valuation_context.title: A median-anchored price clears Veritas's returns hurdle, above its usual multiples
points: 13 comparable deals, all in the same sub-sector, span 19.4x to 23.3x EV/EBITDA with a median of 21.4x. [V:comps]
Margin of 25.0% is above the comps' median of 22.2% but not in the top quarter, so the 50th percentile is the defensible anchor. [V:comps]
Veritas's median paid is 13.7x, yet 5.0x leverage gives a 25.3% IRR at the ask against a 20% target; maximum price is $356M. [V:comps, V:lbo]

risk_flags.title: Size stretch
risk_flags.concern: Median deal of $38M is far below the $300M EV; only 2 of 16 deals sit in the comparable band. [T:record, K:size_band]
risk_flags.mitigant: Its biggest deal was $2,863M and AUM is $50B+, so capacity exists. [T:record, P:2]
risk_flags.reality: Capacity is not the issue; precedent at this size is thin. [K:size_band]

risk_flags.title: Thin sector record
risk_flags.concern: Only 1 deal in the target's own sub-sector, and no open platform there. [T:record, A:angles]
risk_flags.mitigant: The Great Health Informatics bolt-on closed in 2020 at 20.3x. [D:MA-2020-0309]
risk_flags.reality: With no open platform, this would be a stand-alone bet rather than an add-on. [A:angles, C:conviction]

risk_flags.title: Price gap
risk_flags.concern: Its median paid of 13.7x sits well below the 21.4x comparable median. [V:comps]
risk_flags.mitigant: Veritas has paid 21.0x for Great Reimbursement and 20.3x for Great Health Informatics. [D:MA-2022-0294, D:MA-2020-0309]
risk_flags.reality: A median-priced bid means paying above its habit, but the 25.3% IRR at ask leaves room. [V:lbo]

conviction.rationale: Only 1 deal sits in the target's own sub-sector, there is no open platform there, and the $38M median deal is well under the $300M EV. [C:conviction, T:record]
